claims.text: This is the "reuse the import edges, do not recompute them" step.
claims.why: The method uses self._imports which is built from imports_by_file, reusing import edges.

claims.text: The candidate set is the file's own import targets (plus itself), so a resolved type edge always sits on top of an import edge that ``index.py`` already published; a module this file does not import cannot supply a type to it even if the dotted name would match.
claims.why: The method filters rels to those in {importer, *self._imports.get(importer, ())} and then checks if rel is in self._facts.

claims.text: ``pkg/__init__.py`` is named ``pkg.__init__`` by the naming table, but ``from pkg import Thing`` spells the package ``pkg``. Both spellings name the same file, so accepting both is not a guess -- and if a real ``pkg.py`` also exists, the two candidates collide and the name is refused below rather than tie-broken.
claims.why: The code adds an alias by stripping '.__init__' suffix, and the view construction only keeps dotted names with exactly one candidate rel (len(set(rels))==1), so collisions cause exclusion.
